editorial_notes: All delivered mathematical text is the author's own, copied from the pinned publisher source of this unit; no statement or proof step was rewritten, reordered or removed. The counted statement is the author's prop environment at source lines 2450-2459 (printed 8.4) and the counted proof is the proof environment at source lines 2460-2472.

Label adjudication: the counted statement carries the author's own label thm:aexpconcreteu (the label prefix thm notwithstanding, the environment is the author's prop and the publisher prints Proposition); its display carries the author label eq:asymptoticsconcreteunc and the proof's two displays carry the author labels eq:sumIDS and eq:sumIDSsplit; all are delivered with labels renumbered card-locally.

The preamble of the delivered fragment is generated for this unit: the publisher class is replaced by article plus the ams packages, and the author's own package, macro and theorem-declaration lines are retained in source order; publisher meta commands (dates, title, author, address, email, keywords, subject class) are removed.

Reference handling: the counted text's five external pointers are delivered as non-load-bearing stubs citing their published numbers: condI (Condition 7.4), condII (Condition 7.5), condIII (Condition 7.6), condIV (Condition 7.7) from the statement, and eq:asymptoticsconcrete (8.2, source 2422-2427) from the proof.

Citation handling: the proof's two citations are delivered through a one-entry bibliography fragment (bibliography-cited.tex in the card directory) whose item text is copied verbatim from the unit's harvested retained-bibliography.tex (the intake's post-glyph-transcription bibliography file); the author's own printed label [MPS14] is moved into the bibitem optional-label position so the plain citation renders [MPS14] as published.

Citation rendering: the stock LaTeX kernel renders \cite with the label first and the optional note after (kernel macro \@cite prints [LABELS, NOTE]; ltbibl.dtx v1.1t, verified against the kernel source before generation), which is the published cedram order, and the resolved labels come from the bibliography fragment through the aux two-pass (no bibliography backend). \cite{MorParSht2014} therefore renders [MPS14] and \cite[Theorem~2.5]{MorParSht2014} renders [MPS14, Theorem 2.5], both as published; no citation accommodation beyond the fragment is needed. (An earlier draft of this card carried a \renewcommand of \cite to swap note order; it was removed before assembly: the kernel source shows no swap is needed, and a raw-key shim would have printed the cite key instead of the resolved label.)

The published rendering of the counted material and of the stub targets was verified against the publisher PDF of record (Annales Henri Lebesgue 6 (2023), pp. 1031-1113): the proposition prints as Proposition 8.4 (PDF: 'Proposition 8.4. Let A in US_m^alpha be an uncoupleable operator satisfying Conditions 7.4-7.7'), the display inside Theorem 8.2 prints (8.2), and the stub targets print as Conditions 7.4-7.7; the per-section theorem numbering (Theorem 8.1, Theorem 8.2, Remark 8.3 precede this proposition on the shared counter) fixes the counter and all stub numbers.

Notation documentation: BU S_m^{alpha} the author's completely uncoupled system class, pd and mpu the author's macros for 'uncoupleable' and 'competely uncoupleable' (source lines 135 and 2444), N^+- the one-sided counting functions of the IDS, m^+ the number of non-negative summands, v_j the orthonormal splitting vectors of R^2(R^d) tensor C^m, and Conditions I-IV the standing conditions of Section 8. These are documented here rather than stubbed because the counted text invokes them without ref.

The publisher class cedram provides the theorem environments used by the counted text (prop and the proof environment); the generated preamble redeclares them on one section-scoped counter so the delivered statement carries its printed number.

The cedram class front-matter block defining \editors (source lines 172-180, wrapped in \makeatletter/\makeatother) is publisher-class meta machinery: the whitelist strips the \makeatletter wrapper while keeping the \def lines, which would define @-catcode-dependent macros (\editor@name, \editor@string) and reference the cedram conditional \if@francais, none of which exists under the article replacement class; the block is removed with the publisher class and is not referenced by the counted text.
